test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 04
subject: general
question: After giving a discount of 12% on the marked price of a book, a shopkeeper earns a profit of 21%. If he doesn't give this discount, then how much profit would he earn ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for ratio of CP and MP: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

Given Discount (D) = 12% and Profit (P) = 21%.

⇒ CP / MP = (100 − 12) / (100 + 21) = 88 / 121 = 8 / 11

If no discount is given, the item is sold at MP, so SP = 11 and CP = 8.

⇒ Profit % = [(11 − 8) / 8] × 100 = (3 / 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount (D) = 12%

Profit (P) = 21%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%) / 100

SP = MP × (100 − D%) / 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 CP = 100

 
 SP = 121
 
 
 MP = 137.5
 
 
 

 + 21% P
 
 
 

 − 12% D
 
 
 

 New Profit = 37.5%
 
 
 Selling at MP → Profit = MP − CP

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the book be 100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 × (100 + 21) / 100 = 121

The shopkeeper gives a 12% discount on the Marked Price (MP).

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 12) / 100 = MP × 0.88

⇒ 121 = 0.88 × MP

⇒ MP = 121 / 0.88 = 12100 / 88 = 137.5

If no discount is given, the new Selling Price will be equal to the Marked Price.

⇒ New SP = 137.5

⇒ Profit earned = New SP − CP = 137.5 − 100 = 37.5

⇒ Profit % = (37.5 / 100) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is [a + b − (a × b)/100]%. It is always less than the simple sum of the individual discounts.

Direct CP and MP Relation

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price can be directly found using: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This formula bypasses the need for computing the intermediate Selling Price (SP).
